name: Silver Jews
label: Drag City
lede: David Berman and two college friends taped noise in a Hoboken apartment, and the project became the home for his songs. He avoided the stage until 2006, then ended the band in 2009 in a Tennessee cave.

eras.title: Noise from a Hoboken living room
eras.text: Berman met Stephen Malkmus and Bob Nastanovich at the University of Virginia, and the three started taping deliberately bad music in a Hoboken apartment. It began as an art joke. Then Pavement took off, and Silver Jews became the place Berman's writing lived.

years.h: His father's secretary fills out David Berman's UVA application
years.p: Berman starts at the University of Virginia in 1985 and meets Stephen Malkmus and Bob Nastanovich, both later of [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]]. He graduates in 1989 with an English degree.
years.xp:
Berman was born January 4, 1967, in Williamsburg, Virginia. His parents divorced when he was seven; his father, Richard, moved to Dallas to work as a lobbyist and his mother to Wooster, Ohio, to teach.

At UVA he also met James McNew, later of Yo La Tengo, and the four formed a band called Ectoslavia.

years.h: Silver Jews start as a conceptual-art joke in Hoboken
years.p: Berman, Malkmus and Nastanovich record noisy tapes in their apartment in Hoboken, New Jersey. Berman later said the name came from a Silver Jewelry billboard.
years.xp: The name began as a conceptual-art pseudonym and stuck. Berman later called it "a very burdensome band name", since by his own account he was a Jew by patrilineal descent only.

years.src: Wikipedia: David Berman · Wikipedia: Silver Jews
years.h: Two Whitney Museum guards plan a record that looks like a record
years.p: In the early 1990s Berman and Malkmus work as security guards at the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York. Berman said the art on the walls fed his lyrics.
years.xp: Berman named Bruce Nauman, Jean-Michel Basquiat and Louise Lawler among the work that got to him, and wrote lyrics and poems on shift. His account of the band's logic: "let's just make this record that looks like a record." The songs on it would be the ones they made at home that sounded terrible.

years.h: The Arizona Record closes out the home-taped years
years.p: Drag City issues the EP in 1993, a year after Dime Map of the Reef. The early singles and EPs were later gathered on Early Times (2012).

eras.title: Pavement's side project, Berman's whole life
eras.text: In the mid-90s Silver Jews got filed as a Pavement offshoot, since Malkmus and Nastanovich kept turning up. The songs were Berman's, though, and by American Water Pitchfork was handing him a 9.9.

yt: Trains Across the Sea, live in Bloomington, 2006
years.h: Starlite Walker is the first proper album, cut in Memphis
years.p: Recorded in June 1994 at Easley Recordings with Davis McCain and Doug Easley, with Malkmus and Nastanovich still aboard. Berman said Trains Across the Sea was his first original song.

years.h: The Natural Bridge arrives without Malkmus
years.p: Berman makes the second Silver Jews album without Pavement's Stephen Malkmus.

years.h: American Water gets a 9.9 from Pitchfork
years.p: Cut at the Rare Book Room in Brooklyn with Malkmus back on guitar and backing vocals. It opens with Random Rules, and Smith & Jones Forever is track two.
years.xp:
Mike Fellows played bass, Tim Barnes drums, Chris Stroffolino keys and trumpet. Nicolas Vernhes co-produced and the record was mastered at Abbey Road. The working title was The Late, Great Silver Jews, a nod to Townes Van Zandt's The Late Great Townes Van Zandt.

Pitchfork later put it at No. 21 on its list of the 1990s' best albums, with Random Rules at No. 103 on its tracks list. Pitchfork's Matthew Strauss called it "a warm and inviting record" in which Berman "gave in to melody."

years.h: Actual Air sells over 20,000 copies, a lot for poetry
years.p: Open City Books publishes Berman's poetry collection in 1999. Carl Wilson called it even better than Berman's albums.
years.xp: Berman's team marketed the book like a record, and a big share of the sales came through Drag City and record stores rather than bookshops.

years.h: Berman marries Cassie, who owned every Silver Jews record
years.p: David Berman marries Cassie, whom he'd met at a party two years before. He called her the best thing that ever happened to him.
years.xp: Berman said he woke up at her house after the party and found out she owned every Silver Jews album. They lived together in Nashville for 19 years.

eras.title: Nashville, and nearly the end
eras.text: Berman moved to Nashville, brought Cassie into the band, and went through the worst years of his life on the way to Tanglewood Numbers: crack, a suicide attempt, rehab his estranged father paid for, and a turn to Judaism.

years.h: Nashville gives Silver Jews a working band
years.p: Bright Flight, the first Silver Jews album made in Nashville, puts Cassie Berman on vocals, William Tyler on guitar and Tony Crow on keys.

years.h: David Berman wakes up at Vanderbilt three days later
years.p: On November 19, 2003, Berman took crack cocaine, alcohol and tranquilizers intending to die, per Wikipedia. Cassie Berman found him.
years.xp: Berman had been using hard drugs since 1998. He went to rehab afterward, paid for by his father, and said he had not used heroin or cocaine since October 2003. In recovery he took up Judaism and studied the Torah; he later said the faith lasted from 2004 to 2010.

years.cap: Bob Nastanovich and Stephen Malkmus at the Pitchfork Music Festival, Chicago, July 2007
years.h: Tanglewood Numbers survives a studio fire
years.p: The Easley-McCain studio in Memphis, where Silver Jews cut Starlite Walker and where mastering was set, burned down. The tapes survived.
years.xp: The comeback album puts Malkmus and Nastanovich back beside Berman and adds [[Will Oldham|eb51090c-662a-47a1-967c-c63292d9831a]]. William Eggleston's photograph is on the cover.

eras.title: Finally on stage, then gone
eras.text: For its first seventeen years the band barely played live. Sober and newly religious, Berman took it around the world, Israel included, then shut it down with a public letter about his father and one last show in a cave.

yt: Full show, Grey Eagle, Asheville, March 12, 2006
years.h: Seventeen years in, Silver Jews finally tour
years.p: After years of avoiding the stage, the band plays North America and Europe behind Tanglewood Numbers with Brian Kotzur on drums. Israel follows that summer.

years.cap: David and Cassie Berman at Maxwell's, Hoboken, September 2008
years.h: Two nights in Tel Aviv, shot on no budget in three days
years.p: Silver Jews play two Tel Aviv shows and visit Jerusalem. Directors Michael Tully and Matthew Robison film it as Silver Jew.
years.xp: Drag City put out the DVD on September 23, 2008, with an annotated slideshow and music videos for two songs.

years.cap: Silver Jews on stage at Maxwell's, Hoboken, September 8, 2008
years.h: Lookout Mountain, Lookout Sea is the last Silver Jews album
years.p: The band's sixth and final studio album, with Cassie Berman, William Tyler, Tony Crow and Brian Kotzur behind David Berman.

years.big: I always said we would stop before we got bad.
q: I always wanted to go out on top, but I much prefer this.
years.src: Wikipedia: Silver Jews · Wikipedia: David Berman
years.h: Berman ends Silver Jews and names his father
years.p: On Drag City's message board, David Berman reveals his father is lobbyist Richard Berman, and says the band was too small a force to undo his harm.
years.xp:
Berman had been estranged from his father since around 2006. Richard Berman was a Washington lobbyist for the firearms and alcohol industries, among others; this was the first time David named him in public.

He also joked that if he kept recording he might accidentally write the answer song to R.E.M.'s Shiny Happy People, and said he wanted to try screenwriting or muckraking.

years.cap: David Berman at Maxwell's, Hoboken, September 8, 2008, five months before the last show
yt: Smith & Jones Forever, the last song
years.h: The last show is 333 feet underground in a Tennessee cave
years.p: Silver Jews play Cumberland Caverns in McMinnville, Tennessee, for 300 general-admission tickets. The last song is Smith & Jones Forever.
years.xp: The show started at 3 PM. Berman planned to play his 15 favorite Silver Jews songs, and it was shot on 16mm film. A WSM radio broadcast was in the plan until Berman negotiated it out the day before.

eras.title: Purple Mountains
eras.text: A decade after the cave show, Berman came back under a new name with a record about grief and a broken marriage. A month later he was dead.

years.h: Early Times gathers the lo-fi EPs on one record
years.p: Drag City collects the early Silver Jews singles and EPs, including The Arizona Record.

years.h: A Silver Jews reunion photo turns out to be a joke
years.p: A Facebook photo hinting at a reunion gets fans going.

years.h: After 19 years in Nashville, David and Cassie Berman separate
years.p: They never had a fight that ended a marriage, Berman said; they needed to live their lives without each other.
years.xp: Berman described it as not "the kind of conflict that results in divorce." They kept a shared bank account and owned a house together.

years.h: Purple Mountains puts Berman back on record after 11 years
years.p: David Berman returns on Drag City with Purple Mountains, made with members of Woods, and it's hailed as an unexpected second act.
years.xp: Berman said in March 2019 that there had been around 100 nights in the last ten years when he was sure he wouldn't make it to morning. He hoped to tour behind the record to work off about $100,000 in debt from drug use, and he worried depression would get in the way.

years.h: Berman dies at 52, a month after the record comes out
years.p: David Berman died by suicide, by hanging, at an apartment in Park Slope, Brooklyn, on August 7, 2019, according to Wikipedia.
